grade.first_issue: At the terminal board, the proof says that for every prime p the positive-exponent set S_p^* is the singleton {v_p(M)}. This is false when p does not divide M: then S_p^* is empty. The conclusion is repaired immediately by treating that case separately and using the stated convention gcd(∅)=0.
grade.summary: The main proof is correct. Termination follows from the product being nonincreasing, with a strict decrease when the selected gcd exceeds 1, while the count of entries greater than 1 decreases when the product is unchanged. Primewise, the gcd of the positive valuations is invariant under the Euclidean transformation (x,y)↦(min(x,y),|x−y|), which determines every exponent of the unique terminal entry. Only a minor zero-exponent case and a slightly terse descent justification need clarification.
strengths: Correctly identifies the product/count descent governing termination.
Correctly proves that at least one entry greater than 1 always remains.
Correctly derives the prime-valuation transformation under a move.
Correctly identifies the gcd of the positive p-adic valuations as an invariant and reconstructs the terminal integer from it.

errors.description: For primes not dividing the terminal M, S_p^* is empty rather than a singleton; the proof should explicitly invoke the empty-set convention to obtain g_p=v_p(M)=0.

The termination sentence should explicitly use lexicographic descent of (P,C), or state that P never increases and that only finitely many C-decreasing moves can occur between strict decreases of P. This is directly recoverable from the preceding case analysis.
